sheet-1-1.description: The main map of the October 1886 Sanborn sheet of Port Oram, today the borough of Wharton in Morris County, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It covers the centre of the village on both sides of the Morris Canal. South of the canal, Canal street (today Fern Avenue) runs along the towpath side; from it 1st or Main runs south across Poppenhausen (today Central Avenue) towards the school, and 2nd St. runs at a slant from Canal street to Poppenhausen. The large block between them holds the Port Oram Hotel with its horse shed, the post office, a general merchandise store, drug, cigar and confectionery shops and rows of frame dwellings; along Poppenhausen west and east of Main are a hardware and tin shop, a meat market, a hall with a barber and undertaker, a grocery and more dwellings. North of the canal, reached by a wooden bridge at Main, a second Canal street (today Kossuth Avenue) has a wagon shop, a carpenter shop and dwellings, with lumber sheds and yards between it and Top street (today Washington Street), which is lined with dwellings. The High Bridge Branch of the Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the canal west of the bridge, past a coal shed. West of it, beside the canal, stand the Oram, Hance & Co. steam forge with its hammers, forges, blower engine, blacksmith shop, office and a long charcoal house. Block numbers 1 to 7, the legend key, the publisher's title seal and a scale of feet are printed on the sheet. The Port Oram Furnace inset and the Hurd Iron Mine area at the left belong to other parts and are not covered here.
notes: Port Oram is today the borough of Wharton.
Two streets are lettered Canal: the one south of the canal is today Fern Avenue, the one north of it Kossuth Avenue and Kossuth Street.
Top is lettered with the note (Arbitrary), a name given by the publisher; today it is Washington Street.
1st or Main is today North Main Street and South Main Street; Poppenhausen is today West Central Avenue and East Central Avenue.
The Port Oram Furnace is marked not running in October 1886.
Street widths printed: 50 ft for Main and Poppenhausen, 38 ft for 2nd St., 45 ft for Top.

Sanborn, Oct. 1886, 50 ft to an inch, north to upper left (about -21 deg). Part 1 main map: Canal (Fern Av), Top (Washington St), 1st or Main, 2nd St, Poppenhausen (Central Av), Canal north of the canal (Kossuth Av). Part 2: Port Oram Furnace inset (heavy box, own north arrow). Part 3: Hurd Iron Mine area (lower left, own north arrow, 'about 300 ft to the Hurd Iron Mine').

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Port Oram Furnace (blast furnace, casting and stock houses) (no street junction; inset drawn away from its location (about half a mile east of the post office per sheet 2); needs hand-picked control from the furnace site (step 6b), e.g. parcel corners or the DL&W rail spur).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Hurd Iron Mine area with the C.R.R. of N.J. High Bridge Branch (no street junction; drawn about 300 ft from its position ('see below'); needs hand-picked control (step 6b) from the old High Bridge Branch line or the mine site).

sheet-2-1.description: The main map of the 1886 Scarlett & Scarlett sheet of Port Oram (Newark, N.J., copyright 1886), today the borough of Wharton in Morris County, a different survey from the Sanborn sheet of the same year. Drawn at about 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, it covers the village centre south of the Morris Canal: Canal Street along the top, First Street and Second Street running south from it, and Poppenhausen Street crossing both, with Alfred at the lower right where the drawing ends. Blocks are numbered 1 to 6. Along First Street stand Oram Hance & Co.'s general store with the post office, the Port Oram Hotel with its horse shed and wagon house, a drug store, candy and toy shop, cobbler, grocery and a doctor's office; Canal Street is lined with tenements and dwellings, and Second Street has more tenements and dwellings. Poppenhausen Street has a tin ware and stove shop, a hall with meat market, tenements and a grocery. South of Poppenhausen the old school, marked not used, and the public school stand by a vacant lot, and First Street continues south as a dashed road. A large north arrow lies across block 2, and the title cartouche, population note (602) and water facilities note are printed at the top. The lot lines are drawn sparsely and several street edges only as dashed lines, so street positions on this sheet are less exact than on the Sanborn sheet.
notes: Port Oram is today the borough of Wharton.
Canal Street is today Fern Avenue; First Street is North Main Street and South Main Street; Second Street is 2nd Street; Poppenhausen Street is West Central Avenue and East Central Avenue.
Alfred is not identified with a modern street.
Published by Scarlett & Scarlett, Newark, not by Sanborn; bound in the same record as the Sanborn sheet of October 1886.
Poppenhausen Street is lettered 45 ft wide west of First Street.

Scarlett & Scarlett (Newark), 1886, a different survey of the same village; about 50 ft to an inch, north to upper left. Part 1 main map (Canal, First, Second, Poppenhausen Streets, Alfred; blocks 1-6). Part 2: Port Oram Furnace, Jos. Wharton (block 7, own arrow). Part 3: Orchard Mine (iron), James Cooper Lord Estate (block 8, own arrow). Part 4: lower strip along the Morris Canal: Furnace Avenue (Kossuth Av), Washington Street, Oram Hance lumber yard, Port Oram Mnfg Co iron works (blocks 9-10).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: Port Oram Furnace, Jos. Wharton (block 7) (no street junction; about half a mile east of the post office; needs hand-picked control (step 6b) at the furnace site).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: Orchard Mine (iron), James Cooper Lord Estate (block 8) (no street junction; needs hand-picked control (step 6b), e.g. near Orchard Street).

sheet-2-4.description: The lower strip of the 1886 Scarlett & Scarlett sheet of Port Oram, today Wharton, Morris County, showing the north bank of the Morris Canal between the iron works west of Main Street and Washington Street. It is drawn at about 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, at nearly the same angle as the main map but placed on the sheet away from it. Along the canal runs the tow path, crossed by a wooden bridge where the road (today North Main Street) comes up from the south and curves north-east past the Central Railroad of New Jersey, whose High Bridge Branch crosses the canal on its own bridge beside a coal dump roof. Furnace Avenue runs along the canal, with a wheelwright and blacksmith, a carpenter and tenements on its canal side, and Oram Hance & Co.'s lumber yard with its lumber house and piles on the other. Washington Street runs north from Furnace Avenue past stores, a depot and tenements in block 9. At the left, block 10 holds the Port Oram Mnfg Co. iron works: a forge shop with trip hammers, refining and scrap fires, blast engine, furnace, coke house, office and weight house and a long charcoal house, with a note that the works were being made ready to resume. A north arrow, a scale of feet and street widths (26 and 44 ft for Washington Street) are printed in the strip.
notes: Furnace Avenue is today Kossuth Avenue; Washington Street keeps its name.
The road from the wooden bridge, lettered only Road, is today North Main Street.
The Port Oram Mnfg Co. iron works appear on the Sanborn sheet of the same year as the Oram, Hance & Co. steam forge.
Placed from two junctions only (helmert); the North Main Street junction is drawn with dashed edges.
